rules: Import `ruststream_pulsar::prelude::*` in a routes file; a handler body imports `ruststream::prelude::*` alone, except a body that names `partition_key`, which imports this crate's prelude too.

Name a `PulsarSubscription` in `#[subscriber(..)]` whenever the handler needs a setting: `new` for one topic, `topics([..])` for a fixed list, `pattern(..)` for every matching topic, with `subscription_type`, `ack_timeout` and `batch_wait` on it.

`#[subscriber("orders")]` is the short form and opens a `Shared` subscription on that topic under the name set with `PulsarBroker::default_subscription(..)`, and on a broker that sets none it does not compile; in tests set the same `PulsarTestBroker::default_subscription(..)`; a cap and a dead-letter topic declared on it reach that consumer, and every other setting needs a descriptor.

Cap redeliveries with `.max_attempts(n).dead_letter(topic)` right after `include`, always both steps and only on a `Shared` or `KeyShared` subscription (Pulsar counts redeliveries nowhere else), and let the Pulsar client move the spent delivery; `.out_retry(..)` does not compile on this broker.

Set the partition key with the `partition_key` step of the publish builder, bounding the slot `Out<impl Publisher<Options = PulsarPublishOptions>, Marker>`, or write the `partition-key` header for the portable spelling; the key picks the partition of a partitioned topic.

Publish and reply through the `Publish` policy (`out_reply(Publish)`, `.out(Marker, Publish).build()`); the client has no transactions and no reply inbox, so a request/reply exchange is an ordinary publish to another topic.

Open a subscription at a position with `start_at(PulsarPosition::..)` and reposition it from a handler through the `SeekHandle` context key; `start_at` seeks on every startup and rewinds the subscription's durable cursor.
Ask for a batch with `.batch(n)` at the mount site and set `batch_wait` on the descriptor; the Pulsar client delivers one message at a time, so the batch is assembled in the service.
Build a topic name with `PulsarTopic::persistent`/`non_persistent` for literals and `PulsarTopic::parse` for untrusted input, rather than passing a raw string and letting the broker reject it.
Test a service with `ruststream::testing::TestApp` over `PulsarTestBroker` (feature `testing`), mounting the same descriptor and the same `Publish` policy the service ships.
